Lift truck business.heading: Lift Truck Business
Lift truck business.text:
The Company estimates that the global lift truck bookings market slightly improved in Q1 2025 compared to the prior year.

The Lift Truck business experienced a substantial increase in Q1 2025 bookings, predominately in Americas and EMEA. Bookings of $590 million increased 48% sequentially and 13% year-over-year. This improvement was driven by heightened demand for higher-priced, Class 4 and 5 products including the Company's new modular, scalable lift trucks.

These results highlight early signs of lift truck booking market recovery, especially in EMEA. The Lift Truck business remains well-positioned to capture additional market share across its product portfolio, reinforcing its long-term strategic goals. The market is expected to stabilize and improve across 2025, absent the potential effects from tariffs, which we believe caused order hesitation in April.

Lift truck business.heading: Lift Truck Business
Lift truck business.text:
During Q3 2025, the total lift truck market contracted in all geographic regions and classes compared to Q2 2025, reflecting a more cautious customer approach amid ongoing economic uncertainty. The Company believes many customers are deferring capital expenditure, resulting in delayed purchasing decisions and a temporary softening in lift truck order activity.

Despite the broader lift truck market contraction, the Company experienced an uptick in booking activity, with improvements over both the prior year and previous quarter. A portion of this dollar increase is attributable to the increased pricing on the Company’s trucks due to tariff-related material cost increases.

Dollar value bookings improved to $380 million, up from $330 million in the prior quarter, driven by gains in both the EMEA and JAPIC regions, while bookings in the Americas remained stable at relatively low levels. Bookings improved across all product classes.

gp.text: Gross margins are expected to improve gradually from Q2 2026 levels as production volumes increase and pricing and sourcing actions offset a portion of recent tariff costs. The Company's newly introduced low-intensity trucks are expected to contribute favorably to margins while expanding the addressable market and increasing manufacturing scale. However, competitive pricing, particularly in South America and Europe, where competitors continue to compete aggressively with lower-priced value and standard products, is expected to limit the pace of margin improvement. As a result, the Company is maintaining a disciplined approach to balance market share growth and profitability.

intro.text: Hyster-Yale, Inc. ("Hyster-Yale" or the "Company") and its subsidiaries, including its operating companies, Hyster-Yale Materials Handling, Inc. ("HYMH") and Bolzoni S.p.A. ("Bolzoni"), is a globally integrated company offering a full line of high-quality, application-tailored lift trucks and solutions aimed at meeting the specific materials handling needs of its customers. The Company's solutions include attachments, parts, fleet management services, technology and energy solutions. The Company is headquartered in Cleveland, Ohio. Through HYMH, the Company designs, engineers, manufactures, sells and services a comprehensive line of lift trucks, attachments, parts, fleet management services, technology and energy solutions marketed globally, primarily under the Hyster ® , Yale ® and Nuvera® brand names, mainly to independent Hyster ® and Yale ® retail dealerships.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Wages, services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Pension and retiree benefits
lines.why: Promised to employees for their work: operating (some analysts treat the unfunded part as debt).

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.
